Hemangioma of the bone: The patient's presentation of a well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone with preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge, along with MRI findings of isointensity to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images, is consistent with a hemangioma of the bone. The presence of internal hyperintense foci on T1 images, presumed to represent bone marrow fat, further supports this diagnosis.
Fibrous dysplasia: The lesion's location in the diploic space, its well-defined borders, and the presence of a slight bony bulge without disruption of the inner or outer tables could also be consistent with fibrous dysplasia. However, the presence of internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images and the heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images are more typical of hemangioma.
